Subject: POC prompt dataset and eval plan 	6 next steps

Hi Alex / Sara,

Thanks again for the 30-min call this morning 	6 really helpful to hear how Acme is thinking about summarization quality and hallucination risk for the customer support assistant. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a short recap + proposed next steps for the POC so we can align on success criteria and data handoff.

Recap (from our notes):
- Goal: Replace rule-based responses with an LLM-assisted support assistant for Tier 1 and Tier 2 tickets.
- Primary success criteria:
  - Intent classification accuracy >= 92% on sampled prompts
  - Response correctness (factual accuracy) >= 95% on a 200-example eval set
  - Latency: 95th percentile <= 600ms for single-turn generation under expected load
- Data scope: 5k anonymized support prompts + historical agent responses (customer will provide a 1k sample for initial eval)

Proposed POC plan / ownership:
1) Prompt Dataset collection (owner: Acme) 	6 you provide CSV of ~1k representative prompts + agent responses and any redaction notes. See attached sample format.
2) Eval plan & success criteria (owner: Redwood: Marissa + Dev) 	6 we'll produce an eval harness and rubric, then run the 1k sample -> 200-item stratified eval set.
3) Run & iterate (owner: Redwood + Acme) 	6 baseline runs, two rounds of prompt tuning / template adjustments, then final evaluation.
4) Timeline: kick-off this week, initial eval within 10 business days of dataset receipt, final POC results within 4 weeks.

Next concrete asks for Acme:
- Share a trimmed CSV of 800-1,200 prompts + agent replies (see filename example: acmecorp_prompt_samples.csv)
- Highlight any fields we should not use (PII, account IDs) and confirm redaction rules
- Point contact for technical handoff (SFTP / Google Drive) and procurement contact for the SOW

I've attached the updated POC eval plan (poc_eval_plan_v2.pdf) with the rubric and the sample CSV schema. Once we have the dataset we'll: (a) validate format & redaction, (b) generate the stratified eval set, (c) run baseline, and (d) share a short results deck.

Would you be able to share the sample CSV and your preferred file transfer method by EOD Thursday (23 Jul)? If that timeline is tight, let us know and we can adjust.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(650) 555-0123

Attachment(s): poc_eval_plan_v2.pdf, sample_prompt_schema.csv

Subject: Re: POC prompt dataset and eval plan 	6 next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap and plan. This all looks good from our side. Quick answers and next steps:

- We can assemble a first-pass CSV of ~1k prompts and agent responses. I'm attaching a redacted sample (acmecorp_prompt_samples.csv) so you can validate formatting.
- Redaction: we will remove PII and replace account IDs with <ACCOUNT_ID>. We'll also remove any customer emails and contract numbers. Confirm this is acceptable.
- Transfer: we prefer a Google Drive link for the initial batch; I'll upload and share folder access by EOD Thursday.
- Procurement: procurement@acmecorp.com will need the SOW / pricing to start the internal approval. Rafael - looping you so we can coordinate the SOW template.

A couple of clarifying points on success criteria:
- For response correctness, are you expecting automated labels only, or will Redwood provide a human-in-the-loop review for the 200-sample gold set?
- Can you call out how you'll measure hallucination vs. partial correctness?

We're excited to see the baseline and will aim to get the dataset uploaded on Thursday.

Regards,
Alex
Director, Support Automation | AcmeCorp
alex.johnson@acmecorp.com

Attachment(s): acmecorp_prompt_samples.csv

Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC prompt dataset and eval plan 	6 next steps

Thanks Alex 	6 this is great. Confirming the plan and answering your questions:

- Redaction: <ACCOUNT_ID> placeholders and removal of PII is perfect. We only need to know which fields were redacted (a one-line column note is fine).
- Human review: Redwood will perform the automated metrics (intent accuracy, token-level measures) and then a human-in-the-loop judgement for the 200-sample gold set. Our rubric (see poc_eval_plan_v2.pdf) includes binary correctness, hallucination flag, and severity. We will supply the review team and share the human labels in the results workbook.
- Hallucination measurement: we'll use the rubric to categorize (no hallucination / minor hallucination / factual error) and compute a weighted correctness score. Details are in the eval plan; happy to highlight in the kickoff call.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Dev and I will validate the CSV once you upload and will run a format check within 24 hours.
- We'll generate the 200-sample stratified eval set (owner: Redwood) and share the sampling strata for your review.
- Timeline: if we get the CSV on Thu 23 Jul, baseline run by Mon 3 Aug, interim results by Wed 5 Aug, final POC deck by Fri 14 Aug.

Owner contacts:
- Technical lead (Redwood): Dev Patel (dev.patel@redwoodinference.com) 	6 will handle ingestion and runbooks.
- Commercial/SOW: Rafael Mendes (rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com).

Would love to do a short 20-min kickoff call on Friday to align on transfer method and redaction confirmation. Is 10:00am PT ok for you?

Best,

Marissa
